name: Descension

card.summary: Looksmaxxing term for a person's appearance getting worse over time, used to compare before-and-after photos and to track which habits or changes made a face or physique look different.
card.note: A community label and photo-thread format rather than a clinical concept; judgments of 'worse' are subjective.

quick.overview:
Descension is looksmaxxing slang for a decline in how someone looks between two points in time, the opposite of 'ascension'. It is usually shown with side-by-side photos, for example an adolescent photo against a current one, or a before and after a lifestyle change.

The appearance payoff is diagnostic: by lining up dated photos, people try to spot which variable moved (weight, skin, hair, sun exposure, a medication, posture or lighting) and then target that variable. No clinical research uses the term in this sense; it is a forum convention.
quick.how: Users post dated photo sets in threads titled with the word, often asking others to 'rate' the change. Common comparisons span years (for example 2021 to 2024) or are tied to an event such as a medication start, a sunburn, weight change or hair loss. Participants also argue about whether an apparent change is real or due to camera lens, lighting, angle or expression.
quick.risks: Descension threads can be emotionally heavy for posters and readers, and appearance judgments made from photos are unreliable because of lens distortion, lighting and angle. Nothing is ingested or done to the body by the practice itself; the risks lie in the habits or interventions blamed for the change, and in the distress such threads can cause.

lead: Descension is a term in looksmaxxing communities for a person's looks getting worse over time. It is the counterpart of ascension, the community's word for improving one's looks, and it is most often seen in forum threads that present before-and-after photographs and ask other members to rate the difference [1][2].

Its use for appearance is a slang adaptation: elsewhere in the literature the word 'descension' appears only in unrelated technical senses, such as descent of an organ or of a nerve in anatomical and medical papers.

The practice helps people improve how they look in an indirect way. By comparing dated photos, members try to work out what changed (body fat, skin condition, hair density, tan or sun damage, medication, sleep, or simply photo conditions) and then decide what to address. Posters in these threads attribute descension to causes such as sun exposure, weight gain, hair loss treatments and steroid use [3][4][5].

chain: Compare dated photos of the same person
Identify what changed (weight, skin, hair, sun, lighting)
Target the cause or rule out photo artifacts
angle.text: Descension threads serve as a record of how a face or physique changed and what was happening at the time. Members use them to link changes to habits or treatments and to debate whether a change is real or a lens and lighting effect [3][6].

infobox: Weight change, sun exposure, hair loss, medication, steroids, age

paras: In looksmaxxing slang a person 'descends' when their appearance is judged to have declined and 'ascends' when it improves. Threads titled 'my descension' typically show photographs from a younger age beside current ones, sometimes with a short backstory [1][2].
Titles often use superlatives and span specific periods, such as a change between 2021 and 2024 or a change over a few weeks, and some ask readers to rate the person at an earlier age [3][4].

Posters name a range of causes. One thread blames sun exposure for a woman's change in appearance [5]. Another is framed around the look of a person who used anabolic steroids over seven years [6]. A third links changes to a hair-loss medication course and collagen changes while pursuing hairline treatment [7].

Community members also name ordinary factors such as weight gain and aging, and some argue the supposed change is a lens or lighting effect rather than a real difference; one thread is titled to the effect that lens distortion cannot explain a given descension [8].
No studies found. The word 'descension' appears in the medical literature only in unrelated anatomical and clinical senses, such as descent of the testis or of a nerve, and not for appearance change.

Descension threads are a staple of the community's photo-rating culture. Proponents of the format say seeing change documented helps motivate corrective action and shows which interventions matter. Critics within the same forums point to photo conditions as a confound, and replies in these threads range from supportive to harsh [1][8].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, descension threads present photo comparisons and argue about causes [1][3].

claims.claim: Sun exposure can cause a rapid, visible decline in looks.
claims.believers: Posters attribute a sudden worsening in a person's appearance to time in the sun [5].
claims.experts: Dermatology research describes photoaging as cumulative ultraviolet damage; no published study uses the descension framing.

claims.claim: Apparent descension is sometimes a camera or lens effect.
claims.believers: Members argue that focal length, angle and lighting can exaggerate differences between photos [8].
claims.experts: No published study has tested this claim in the context of forum photo threads.

claims.claim: Steroid or drug use can age the face noticeably within years.
claims.believers: A thread frames a physique and face change over seven years as 'roidcel' descension [6].
claims.experts: No published study has evaluated forum-reported cases of this kind.
